sandhi.note: The prefixes उप and आ fuse: a + ā → ā.
Final m before a consonant is written as anusvāra; likewise देवीं दैत्यानाम्.
Final t stays unvoiced before t; the words are written together.

sandhi.type: consonant joined to vowel; vowel sandhi inside a compound (guṇa)
sandhi.note: The m joins the next vowel; inside the compound अधिप + ईश्वर → अधिपेश्वर (a + ī → e).

samasa.literal: that on which (there are) a hundred moons
samasa.sense: a shield studded with a hundred moon-shaped bosses
with दैत्यानाम्: the lord over the chiefs of the Daityas
samasa.alt: Also a karmadhāraya, अधिपः चासौ ईश्वरः च, ‘the sovereign overlord’; with the genitive दैत्यानाम् the sense is nearly the same.

morph.note: Absolutive of उप + आ + √दा ‘to take up’: with a prefix the absolutive ends in -य (ल्यप्), not -त्वा.
Imperfect active of अभि + √धाव्: the augment comes after the prefix (अभि + अ + धावत् → अभ्यधावत्). The same verb appears in the middle, अभ्यधावत, in 10.25.

mantras.anvaya: ततः दैत्यानाम् अधिपेश्वरः खड्गं भानुमत् शतचन्द्रं च उपादाय तदा देवीम् अभ्यधावत्।
mantras.anvaya_en: An absolutive phrase (खड्गं … शतचन्द्रं च उपादाय) and the main clause: अधिपेश्वरः देवीम् अभ्यधावत्.
mantras.lit: Then, taking up a sword and a shining shield marked with a hundred moons, the lord of the Daityas’ chiefs then rushed at the Goddess.
mantras.tr: Then the overlord of the Daityas took up a sword and a gleaming shield adorned with a hundred moons, and charged at the Goddess.
mantras.tr_note: ततः and तदा both mean ‘then’; the second is not repeated in tr.

comm.t: With bow and spear gone, Śumbha closes in with sword and shield. शतचन्द्र, ‘hundred-moon’, is the Epic name for a shield decorated with moon-shaped ornaments; भानुमत् ‘shining’ describes it.

For अभ्यधावत्तदा देवीं other witnesses read अभ्यधावत तां देवीं (GRETIL, Freund): the middle form of the verb with the pronoun ताम् instead of the adverb तदा. The meaning is unchanged; the Gita Press reading is kept.

flags.uncertain: Variant (corrections.json, status ‘Textual Verification Required’): अभ्यधावत तां देवीं for अभ्यधावत्तदा देवीं (GRETIL, Freund). The Gita Press reading is analysed.

a + a → ā; the same inside the compound (अर्ककर + अमल).
The s of धनुस् appears as r before the voiced m.

samasa.alt: Also tṛtīyā tatpuruṣa, धनुषा मुक्ताः, ‘released by the bow’; the sense is the same.

samasa.vigraha: अर्ककराः इव अमलम्; अर्कस्य कराः अर्ककराः
samasa.type: upamāna-pūrvapada karmadhāraya, containing a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa (अर्ककर)
samasa.literal: spotless like the rays of the sun
samasa.alt: Also ‘bright with the sun’s rays’ (अर्ककरैः अमलम्, tṛtīyā tatpuruṣa), of a polished shield that reflects the sun.

morph.note: Present participle of आ + √पत् ‘to fly at, rush on’, genitive singular, agreeing with तस्य: ‘of him rushing on’. With एव: ‘just as he was rushing on’.
Nominative-accusative singular neuter of चर्मन् (the final n is lost): ‘hide’, hence a leather shield — here the शतचन्द्र of 10.16.

mantras.anvaya: आपततः एव तस्य खड्गं चण्डिका आशु चिच्छेद, धनुर्मुक्तैः शितैः बाणैः अर्ककरामलं चर्म च (चिच्छेद)।
mantras.anvaya_en: Subject चण्डिका, verb चिच्छेद with two objects: खड्गम् (with तस्य आपततः एव and आशु) and चर्म (with its instrument बाणैः and qualifier).
mantras.lit: Even as he was rushing on, Caṇḍikā swiftly cut his sword, and with sharp arrows shot from the bow (she cut) his shield, spotless as the sun’s rays.
mantras.tr: As he rushed in, Caṇḍikā swiftly cut his sword in two, and with keen arrows from her bow she split his shield, bright as sunlight.

comm.t: Sword and shield go together. The first half-line is the formula already used for Niśumbha in 9.33 (तस्यापतत एवाशु गदां चिच्छेद चण्डिका, there with the club): the Goddess strikes before the blow can land.

Other witnesses (GRETIL, Freund) add a third line here: अश्वांश्च पातयामास रथं सारथिना सह, ‘and she brought down his horses, and the chariot with the charioteer’. It is not in the Gita Press text, whose colophon count (27 ślokas and one half-śloka) agrees with the two-line form. The line would explain the next verse, where Śumbha is suddenly ‘horseless’ and ‘charioteerless’.

flags.uncertain: Recension variant (corrections.json, status ‘recension’): GRETIL and Freund add a third line, अश्वांश्च पातयामास रथं सारथिना सह. Not in the Gita Press text; not analysed.

samasa.literal: ready for the death of Ambikā

morph.note: Perfect of √ग्रह्: the reduplicated syllable takes samprasāraṇa (ग्र → गृ), its ṛ becomes a, and the guttural becomes the palatal ज: ज-ग्राह.
Nominative singular masculine of the n-stem धन्वन्, which replaces धनुस् at the end of a bahuvrīhi.

mantras.anvaya: तदा हताश्वः छिन्नधन्वा विसारथिः अम्बिकानिधनोद्यतः सः दैत्यः घोरं मुद्गरं जग्राह।
mantras.anvaya_en: The subject दैत्यः carries five qualifiers (हताश्वः, सः, छिन्नधन्वा, विसारथिः, अम्बिकानिधनोद्यतः); the verb is जग्राह with the object मुद्गरम्.
mantras.lit: Then that Daitya — horses slain, bow cut, without charioteer — intent on the death of Ambikā, seized a dreadful mace.
mantras.tr: Then the Daitya, his horses killed, his bow cut, his charioteer gone, still bent on killing Ambikā, seized a dreadful mace.

comm.t: Śumbha has lost chariot horses, bow and charioteer; he fights on, now on foot, with a mace. In the Gita Press text the loss of horses and charioteer is stated only here, by the compounds; the extra line found in other witnesses at 10.17 narrates it.
A modern reading: three compounds strip the king, one loss at a time — yet the last compound is his unchanged intent (अम्बिकानिधनोद्यतः). Nothing that is taken from him alters his purpose.

Nominative singular masculine of वेगवत्, ‘possessing speed’ (possessive suffix मतुप्, v after a-stems).

mantras.anvaya: आपततः तस्य मुद्गरं (देवी) निशितैः शरैः चिच्छेद। तथा अपि वेगवान् सः मुष्टिम् उद्यम्य ताम् अभ्यधावत्।
mantras.anvaya_en: Two sentences. The first has an understood subject (the Goddess, from 10.17); the second: सः … ताम् अभ्यधावत्, with the absolutive phrase मुष्टिम् उद्यम्य.
mantras.lit: (She) cut, with sharpened arrows, the mace of him as he was rushing on. Even so he, impetuous, raising his fist, rushed at her.
mantras.tr: As he charged, she cut his mace apart with keen arrows; even so he rushed at her, fist raised, in his fury.

comm.t: The last weapon is gone; Śumbha attacks with his bare fist. The pattern of 10.17 is repeated: the weapon is cut ‘as he rushes on’, before the blow.
A modern reading: the text gives the demon no surrender. The narrative of 10.14–19 removes every instrument he has, and he keeps coming with his hands.

samasa.sense: the foremost of the Daityas — पुङ्गव ‘bull’ at the end of a compound means ‘chief, best’
samasa.alt: Also an upamita karmadhāraya, दैत्यः पुङ्गवः इव, ‘a Daitya like a bull’; the conventional sense ‘chief’ is the same.

morph.note: Periphrastic perfect: the causative stem पातय- + आम्, followed by the perfect of √अस् (आस). Causative stems form their perfect only in this way.
Imperfect of the curādi root √तड् (stem ताडय-): augment अ + ताडय + त्.

mantras.anvaya: सः दैत्यपुङ्गवः देव्याः हृदये मुष्टिं पातयामास। सा देवी च अपि तलेन तम् उरसि अताडयत्।
mantras.anvaya_en: Two clauses: Śumbha’s blow (सः … मुष्टिं पातयामास, with हृदये देव्याः) and the Goddess’s (सा देवी … तम् उरसि अताडयत्). देव्याः, printed at the head of the second line, belongs with हृदये in the first clause.
mantras.lit: He, the bull among the Daityas, brought down his fist on the heart of the Goddess. And she, the Goddess, in turn struck him on the chest with her palm.
mantras.tr: The mightiest of the Daityas brought his fist down on the Goddess’s heart; and she in turn struck him on the chest with the flat of her hand.

comm.t: Śumbha’s fist reaches the Goddess’s heart. Her answer is an open-handed blow (तलेन) to his chest, which fells him (10.21).
A modern reading: fist against open palm — the narrative contrasts his clenched effort with her unclenched hand, and the open hand is the stronger.
